Hi Lina — thanks for the materials and the clear list. Looping Ben from Commercial to cover marketplace-specific billing notes; Vanessa handles our marketplace activation flow.

High-level intake steps (what we'll do on our side):
1) Intake form + vendor docs: please upload your W-9 and bank stub to the Drive folder I created (link below). That lets Finance validate tax ID and banking.
2) Vendor record creation: once W-9 validated, Finance creates a vendor record (this is separate from marketplace billing).
3) Marketplace routing:
   - AWS Marketplace: billing typically goes through AWS (they invoice the buyer). We still require the vendor entity for payout setup and marketplace listing configuration.
   - GCP Marketplace: similar flow, but depending on listing type we may need a direct contract for revenue share.
4) PO routing options:
   - If you're buying via AWS/GCP marketplace: generate PO to the marketplace channel (we'll accept marketplace POs; no direct Redwood PO required for consumption billing).
   - If you want Redwood to be the payee (Direct Dedicated solution or enterprise contract): Redwood Finance requires a PO referencing Redwood Inc. and our vendor tax ID.

A couple of asks for faster turnaround:
- Confirm legal entity name for invoicing (exact spelling and remit address).
- Provide primary AP contact and an AP email for PO communications.
- Confirm desired payment terms (Net30/Net45).

I've created a short intake checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcProcureOnboarding (drop the W-9 there). Our expected SLAs: vendor record + marketplace mapping within 2 business days after receiving validated W-9.

Thanks — I'll open an intake ticket once I have the documents.

Hey all — quick operational notes from Commercial / Sales ops side to clarify marketplace behavior: 

1) AWS Marketplace (SaaS Subscriptions):
   - The buyer submits a PO to AWS; AWS invoices the buyer. AWS then remits to the seller. Redwood will need a seller payout profile for your entity to make the listing live.
   - For tracking, include your internal PO number in the purchase line item; AWS will surface that in invoices. No additional vendor code is required unless the buyer asks for us to add it in metadata.
2) GCP Marketplace:
   - GCP has two billing models — marketplace-managed billing (similar to AWS) and direct billing (contract). If you want the easiest path, marketplace-managed billing is recommended.
3) Direct Redwood billing (Dedicated/Enterprise):
   - We'll require a Redwood PO recipient vendor record. Finance will issue NRAs for onboarding and map to our AR system.

Operational ask: Lina/Jordan — please confirm the vendor tax ID (EIN) so Finance can create the vendor record. Once vendor record is created, vendor activation for AWS/GCP listings is straightforward (we push the marketplace config and request payout verification).

Link to our internal procurement playbook (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcProcureOnboarding

If you prefer, Mina or I can run a 20-minute sync with your AP to walk through PO examples.

Cheers,
